question: In view of the serious railway accident of 18 January 2026 in Adamuz, Andalusia, the European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) must launch an investigation into the tragedy, which happened, sadly, 12 years on from the Alvia train crash in Santiago de Compostela – the Angrois accident.

In 2016, I lodged a complaint with the Commission so that it would open infringement proceedings against Spain, having uncovered shortcomings in the way in which the Spanish State conducted the investigation into the accident: the investigation was carried out by a body proven not to be independent, it failed to provide protection and transparency for the victims and it was shrouded in government opacity.

Spain’s well-known failure to apply European railway safety standards was corroborated by the Commission’s decision to open infringement proceedings in 2018, which were closed in 2024 following much delay and obstruction by the Spanish State. 1.
Can the Commission confirm whether an ERA investigation has now been opened following the Adamuz accident of 18 January 2026?
Will the Commission open infringement proceedings against Spain in connection with this latest tragedy?
Can the Commission ascertain whether the rules implemented following the Angrois accident were being applied at the time of the tragic Adamuz accident?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.4.2026) The Commission regrets the tragic loss of life following the rail accidents near Adamuz. In relations to the three questions put to it, the Commission recalls the following: 1. Under EU railway safety Directive (EU) 2016/798 (the Directive)1, the responsibility for investigating railway accidents independently lies with national investigation bodies (NIBs).

The EU Agency for Railways (ERA) can offer technical assistance according to Article 22(5) of the Directive and did so immediately. On that basis, ERA will observe and assist on the work of the investigative body CIAF2. 2. Any decision concerning possible infringement proceedings in relation to the Adamuz rail accident is conditional on the conclusion of the ongoing investigation and on its findings.

The Commission decided in March 2024 to close the infringement proceedings3 referred to by the Honourable Member because Spain had addressed the systemic weaknesses in the supervision and accident investigation processes following an agreed and supervised action plan with annual reporting to the Commission and ERA. ERA confirmed the significant progress during an audit in 2023. 3.

The Commission will continue monitoring closely the situation while awaiting the findings of the CIAF investigation, to determine if accident in Adamuz could have as a causal factor a flaw in the actions taken within the abovementioned action plan.

The Commission will react, if necessary, using the appropriate instruments of the Rail Safety Directive (EU) 2016/798 to guarantee the highest levels of safety and ensure that each actor fulfils its responsibility towards it.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/798/oj/eng. 2 Comisión de Investigación de Accidentes Ferroviarios. 3 Press release concerning the case: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/memo_19_462.
